From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Cc: dev_patel@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 14 Aug 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap + prompt collection request

Hi Samir,

Great to meet earlier. Quick recap and next steps from our discovery: 

- Primary use case: auto-summarization and classification of customer support tickets
- Volume: ~120k tickets/month, average ticket length ~250 tokens, peak concurrency ~30 reqs/s
- Quality bar: high precision on intents (billing, tech-support, escalation), avoid hallucinations on account-level data
- Data sensitivity: customer emails and account numbers included in some examples

Action items I promised: 
1) Could you share a sample prompt set (real examples or redacted) covering common and edge-case tickets? A simple CSV is fine - one prompt per row with label/context.
2) Mark any fields you'd prefer redacted or token-masked (PII, account numbers, SSNs, internal notes). See our attached redaction guidance for examples.
3) Any existing internal workflows for redaction (pre-send pipeline) or must we provide in-line redaction recommendations?

Recommended attachments I'm sending:
- prompt_set_template.csv (column headers: id, prompt_text, expected_label, notes)
- redaction_guidelines_acme.pdf [Attachment: redaction_guidelines_acme.pdf]

If you can drop a first pass of 50-100 prompts this week, we'll run a quick model-fit eval and share recommended models + a small benchmark.

Thanks — looping in Dev for technical details.


Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Samir — thanks for the file, got it and took a quick look. Helpful stuff. A few immediate recommendations: 

1) Model recommendations (based on initial sample):
   - Cost-conscious baseline: an optimized 7B quantized model (Redwood-7b-q4) - low latency, good enough for intent classification and quick summarization.
   - Quality-first option: Redwood-13b-ft or a 30B variant for improved summarization fidelity and fewer hallucinations.
   - For a canary we recommend starting with the 7B on Dedicated/reserved pool for predictable latency; switch traffic to 13B for higher-quality cohorts.

2) Benchmarks / eval links:
   - Lightweight model-fit report (internal): https://redwood-inference.com/benchmarks/overview
   - Example eval harness (shared Drive): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-prompt-sets

3) Redaction guidance / suggestions:
   - We recommend removing or token-masking: emails, SSNs, bank/account numbers, tokens that map to internal IDs unless necessary for downstream mapping.
   - If you need mapping to persist, consider hashing with a salt stored in your system and pass hashed values to the model.
   - For multi-intent tickets, include a short instruction prefix to the model: "Identify all intents and label each with confidence scores."

Next steps:
- Dev (cc'd) will propose a simple ingestion pipeline for sanitized prompts + a small eval set.
- If you can confirm which fields must remain (account_id vs account_number) we'll include automatic redaction rules in the POC.

I'll schedule a 30-min sync to walk through the benchmark results once we run the initial eval.


Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Hi team — quick technical notes from my side: 

- Ingestion: we can accept CSVs or a JSONL format. For the POC, CSV is easiest; we'll convert to JSONL in the pipeline.
- Automated redaction: we offer an optional pre-processing filter that masks emails/SSNs/account numbers using regex + configurable allowlist. If you prefer, we can run both redacted and unhashed account_id variants in parallel for mapping.
- Batching & latency: with a dedicated 7B q4 pool we expect p50 latency ~80-120ms per request at your projected concurrency with continuous batching enabled.
- Regression monitoring: we'll run prompt-set evaluations (accuracy/precision/recall + hallucination checks) and set an alert if overall F1 drops >5% from baseline. Put your canonical test set in the shared Drive folder and we'll hook it up.

Suggested rollout for POC:
1) Share sanitized 200-500 prompt examples (we have 50 so far)
2) Redwood runs model-fit eval and shares per-model metrics + recommended config
3) 2-week canary on Dedicated 7B pool, monitor quality & cost; if quality gaps persist, open traffic to 13B for a subset of users

I'm attaching an example eval config we use internally and will create a short-run job once you upload the sample set to the Drive link above.


Dev Patel
Principal Engineer, Inference Ops
